name: Benjamini-Yekutieli false discovery allocator
note: Twelve candidate rules drawn from twelve different indicator families run side by side. At each recompute the per-bar return series of every rule is turned into a one-sided Newey-West t for the null of zero mean return, the p-values are sorted, and the Benjamini-Yekutieli step-up procedure with c(M) = sum 1/j - valid under arbitrary dependence, which is the case that matters when the candidates overlap - selects the discovery set at false-discovery rate q. Rules outside the set are silent until the next recompute; if nothing clears, the book is flat. The source's 1/i risk allocation across discoveries becomes an equal-weight vote here, because a single-symbol harness holds one position rather than i of them, and vote_min is how much of the funded book has to agree. c(M)=1 in the grid is plain Benjamini-Hochberg, the positive-dependence-only version, so the sweep prices the Yekutieli correction directly. The source's quarterly cadence is not observable inside an intraday research window, so the recompute is every 250 bars over a 1000-bar evidence window, and the Newey-West lag is the textbook floor(4*(n/100)^(2/9)) = 5 rather than a lag chosen to manufacture significance. Worth knowing before reading its results: on the probe bars this family funds nothing at all on SOXL at any q, window or lag, because no rule's leveraged-ETF return stream reaches significance in a 33-day sample, and it therefore sits flat on that symbol. That is the procedure working, not a broken threshold - but it does mean a flat equity curve here is evidence of abstention, not of a signal that failed.
source: Benjamini, Y. & Hochberg, Y. (1995), 'Controlling the False Discovery Rate', JRSS-B 57(1), 289-300; Benjamini, Y. & Yekutieli, D. (2001), 'The Control of the False Discovery Rate in Multiple Testing under Dependency', Annals of Statistics 29(4), 1165-1188. Applied to trading and factor discovery in Harvey, C., Liu, Y. & Zhu, H. (2016), '...and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns', Review of Financial Studies 29(1), 5-68 (their BHY-implied t-hurdle is 3.39 at FDR 1% as of 2012, versus 3.78 for Holm/FWER 5%).

import math as _m

_SQ2 = _m.sqrt(2.0)
_M = 12


def _phi(x):
    return 0.5 * (1.0 + _m.erf(x / _SQ2))


def family_init(ctx):
    """Twelve candidate rules, one per indicator family. Nothing is read here:
    the harness's look-ahead guard is armed, and the rule series are filled in
    bar by bar from signal() so every read is checked."""
    n = len(ctx.bars)
    ctx.n = n
    ctx.raw_c = [float(b["c"]) for b in ctx.bars]
    ctx.e_f = ctx.indicator("ema", period=9)
    ctx.e_s = ctx.indicator("ema", period=30)
    ctx.rsi = ctx.indicator("rsi", period=14)
    ctx.mac = ctx.indicator("macd", fast=12, slow=26, signal=9)
    ctx.bb = ctx.indicator("bollinger", period=20, mult=2.0)
    ctx.don = ctx.indicator("donchian", period=20)
    ctx.stn = ctx.indicator("supertrend", period=10, mult=3.0)
    ctx.adx = ctx.indicator("adx", period=14)
    ctx.sto = ctx.indicator("stoch", k_period=14, d_period=3)
    ctx.cci = ctx.indicator("cci", period=20)
    ctx.vwp = ctx.indicator("vwap")
    ctx.par = ctx.indicator("psar", step=0.02, max_step=0.2)

    ctx.rsig = [[0] * n for _ in range(_M)]     # each rule's -1/0/+1
    ctx.rret = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(_M)]   # each rule's per-bar return
    ctx.done = -1
    ctx.disc = []
    ctx.nxt = int(ctx.p.est_win)
    ctx.cM = (sum(1.0 / j for j in range(1, _M + 1))
              if int(ctx.p.by_mode) else 1.0)


def _fill(ctx, j):
    """Rule signals on bar j. Every read is at j or j-1."""
    s = [0] * _M
    px = ctx.raw_c[j]
    a, b = ctx.e_f[j], ctx.e_s[j]
    if a is not None and b is not None:
        s[0] = 1 if a > b else -1
    r = ctx.rsi[j]
    if r is not None:
        s[1] = 1 if r < 30 else (-1 if r > 70 else 0)
        s[2] = 1 if r > 55 else (-1 if r < 45 else 0)
    hh = ctx.mac.hist[j]
    if hh is not None:
        s[3] = 1 if hh > 0 else -1
    u, l = ctx.bb.upper[j], ctx.bb.lower[j]
    if u is not None and l is not None:
        s[4] = -1 if px > u else (1 if px < l else 0)
    if j >= 1:
        du, dl = ctx.don.upper[j - 1], ctx.don.lower[j - 1]
        if du is not None and dl is not None:
            s[5] = 1 if px > du else (-1 if px < dl else 0)
    sd = ctx.stn.dir[j]
    if sd is not None:
        s[6] = 1 if sd > 0 else -1
    ax, pd, md = ctx.adx.adx[j], ctx.adx.plus_di[j], ctx.adx.minus_di[j]
    if None not in (ax, pd, md) and ax > 20:
        s[7] = 1 if pd > md else -1
    kk = ctx.sto.k[j]
    if kk is not None:
        s[8] = 1 if kk < 20 else (-1 if kk > 80 else 0)
    cv = ctx.cci[j]
    if cv is not None:
        s[9] = 1 if cv > 100 else (-1 if cv < -100 else 0)
    vw = ctx.vwp[j]
    if vw is not None:
        s[10] = 1 if px > vw else -1
    ps = ctx.par.dir[j]
    if ps is not None:
        s[11] = 1 if ps > 0 else -1

    lg = 0.0
    if j >= 1 and px > 0 and ctx.raw_c[j - 1] > 0:
        lg = _m.log(px / ctx.raw_c[j - 1])
    for k in range(_M):
        ctx.rsig[k][j] = s[k]
        prev = ctx.rsig[k][j - 1] if j >= 1 else 0
        ctx.rret[k][j] = prev * lg


def _recompute(ctx, t):
    """One-sided Newey-West p-value per rule, then the BY step-up."""
    win = int(ctx.p.est_win)
    L = int(ctx.p.nw_lags)
    q = float(ctx.p.q)
    lo = t - win + 1
    if lo < 0:
        lo = 0
    ps = []
    for k in range(_M):
        x = ctx.rret[k][lo:t + 1]
        nn = len(x)
        if nn < 30:
            ps.append((1.0, k))
            continue
        mu = sum(x) / nn
        d = [y - mu for y in x]
        lrv = sum(y * y for y in d) / nn
        for lag in range(1, L + 1):
            gl = 0.0
            for j in range(lag, nn):
                gl += d[j] * d[j - lag]
            lrv += 2.0 * (1.0 - lag / (L + 1.0)) * (gl / nn)
        if lrv <= 0:
            ps.append((1.0, k))
            continue
        se = _m.sqrt(lrv / nn)
        ps.append((1.0 - _phi(mu / se) if se > 0 else 1.0, k))
    ps.sort()
    best = 0
    for r in range(1, _M + 1):
        if ps[r - 1][0] <= (r / (_M * ctx.cM)) * q:
            best = r
    ctx.disc = [k for _, k in ps[:best]]


def signal(ctx, i):
    j = ctx.done + 1
    while j <= i:
        _fill(ctx, j)
        j += 1
    ctx.done = i
    if i >= ctx.nxt:
        ctx.nxt = i + int(ctx.p.cadence)
        _recompute(ctx, i)
    if not ctx.disc:
        return 0
    v = sum(ctx.rsig[k][i] for k in ctx.disc) / float(len(ctx.disc))
    vmin = float(ctx.p.vote_min)
    if v >= vmin:
        return 1
    if v <= -vmin:
        return -1
    return 0
